newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to unveil non-resident T-bill easing May 1.
newsitem.headline: Russia to unveil non-resident T-bill easing May 1.

text.p: The Russian Central Bank will take further steps to liberalise the Treasury bill market starting on May 1, bank deputy chairman Andrei Kozlov said on Wednesday.
But Central Bank Chairman Sergei Dubinin told the Duma lower house of parliament there were no plans to end a 15 percent quota on foreign participation in the domestic government securities market.
Kozlov said the bank intended to effectively end forward deal requirements, the primary mechanism the bank uses to regulate foreign repatriation of T-bill profits, by year end.

"Now foreigners have to use forwards with at least a two-month period to take money from the market, but from January 1 (next year) the time period of the forward will be cut to one to three days," he told a news conference.

He did not give details of the measures considered for May 1 launch but said the bank's credit committee had approved a plan of liberalisation in mid-February and the Board of Directors would consider measures soon.
Dubinin said Russia should still be careful not to let foreign participants take a large part of the market, which would threaten catastrophe should they suddenly leave.
"In terms of additional access by non-residents -- so far there is a very strong Mexican syndrome and the 15 percent quota should hold," he said.
But he said foreign participants had allowed the bank to lower yields on the securities, which yielded near 30 percent on Wednesday, down from close to 200 percent early last year.
"In large part, this (foreign participation) has allowed us to lower yields," he added.
